question: How are François's (2005) charts of vowel hybridization (Appendix 1, pp. 490-491) entered?
chosen_reading: As PNCV > language rows (the 17 Torres and Banks languages and Sakao already sit under PNCV), with five implied PNCV retentions of the POc vowels, since François derives the modern vowels from *i e a o u through changes that happened separately in each language (pp. 456-457). Each cell *V1(C)V2 > V' is a row on the stressed vowel (*V1 > V' / _(C)V2), and each posttonic vowel gets one loss row (*V2 > ∅ after the stressed vowels where it is lost) or, where it survives as a final vowel (Hiu, Lo-Toga, Vera'a, Mota), a row *V2 > Vf / V1(C)_. Several reflexes in a cell are regular with conditioning unknown; angled brackets (adjacent vowels) are rows with the environment '_V2 (adjacent)'. Lo-Toga '(i)ɛ' is entered as ɛ and as the diphthong i͡ɛ; Mota '(i)_e' as *i > i and *i > ∅. Vurës and Sakao ü are y (Sakao's inventory, Crowley 2002, has y for Guy's ü); Mwotlap ɪ, ʊ are e, o, the symbols of its inventory (Lynch et al. 2002). Lehalurup '?' and the empty Nume cell (*u…o) have no rows. Sakao is cited as Guy (1977) via François.
alternatives: Fusion pairs (*V1 + *V2 > V'); rows against POc on a Torres-Banks node; Table 1 vowel inventories as sourced phonemes (they would leave the consonants unsourced).
